article:
## Introduction

Claude’s MCP connectors let you bring live data from tools like Google Drive and many others straight into your chat. This removes the need to copy-paste or switch tabs while you draft campaigns, analyse performance or brainstorm ideas.

## How to access the Connectors Directory

Open Claude or Claude Desktop, click Customize then select Connectors. This opens the directory of available MCP servers where you will see both verified and community connectors listed.

## How to add a connector

Type the name of the service you want, for example Google Drive, to find it in the directory. Select the connector and follow the prompts to allow Claude to access the service.

## How to test the connector

After the window closes, check that the connector is active. To test, open a new chat and ask Claude to fetch a recent file from the service, for example ‘Show me the latest proposal in the Marketing folder’. Claude will return the file name and a snippet, proving the connector works.

## How to repeat for other services

Repeat the same steps for other verified connectors you need. Each appears in the directory. You can have multiple services active at once and switch between them easily in chat.

## What I’d do

I start with Google Drive because it holds most of my briefs and assets. I add it, test it, then add other verified connectors to pull campaign performance data and check upcoming deadlines. Once those are working I feel confident to bring in Notion for content planning and Slack for team updates. The whole process takes less than twenty minutes and gives Claude live access to the data I actually use.

## The best ChatGPT apps and connectors for marketers

Marketers spend too much time jumping between ChatGPT and their tools. The ChatGPT Apps marketplace and verified MCP servers let you bring data from ad platforms, CRMs and automation services straight into the chat. This removes the need to copy-paste or switch tabs while you draft campaigns, analyse performance or brainstorm ideas.

## Why connect apps inside ChatGPT

When you install a verified app or plugin, ChatGPT gains live access to external data. You can ask for real-time keyword volumes, pull CRM records or trigger a Zapier workflow, all from a single conversation. The setup is quick: you need a ChatGPT Plus plan to open up Developer Mode, then you add the app from the Settings → Apps menu.

## Step-by-step: how to switch on the top apps

### Ensure you have ChatGPT Plus

Developer Mode, required for MCP servers, is only available on Plus, Pro, Team, Enterprise and Edu plans. Free plans cannot use MCP servers. The Plus plan starts at $20 per month.

### Open Settings → Apps

In ChatGPT click your name, choose Settings, then select Apps. This opens the marketplace where you can search for verified connectors.

### Add Adspirer for multi-platform ad management

Search for Adspirer, click Connect and authorise your Google, Meta, Amazon, ChatGPT Ads, LinkedIn and TikTok accounts. Adspirer has been an official listing since May 29 2026 and connects to over 400 tools across six platforms. Since June 2026 it returns interactive in-chat dashboards with tabbed Overview, Campaigns and Insights views.

### Add HubSpot plugin for CRM

The HubSpot plugin lets you read contact lists, deal stages and trigger workflows using natural language. It works across claude.ai, Claude Desktop and other ChatGPT surfaces, giving you live CRM data without leaving the chat.

### Add Zapier plugin for workflow automation

With the Zapier plugin you describe an automation, for example “When a new lead arrives in HubSpot, add a row to Google Sheets”, and Zapier builds it inside the chat. You can then run or edit the workflow by conversation.

### Test with a live data prompt

Try a prompt such as “Show me my worst performing campaigns this month” to see real numbers from your ad accounts. The answer appears as an interactive dashboard you can filter by date range.

## What I'd do

I start each week by opening ChatGPT, confirming I have Plus, then adding Adspirer, HubSpot and Zapier in that order. I spend less than five minutes setting up the three connectors. After that I run a quick audit prompt to check ad performance, pull a contact list for outreach and trigger a follow-up sequence in Zapier. The whole process stays inside one chat window, saving me tabs and reducing context-switching.

## Connect Instagram to Claude using MCP

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) lets AI apps like Claude talk directly to external services such as Instagram without handling OAuth or API keys yourself. Two guides published in early October 2026 show how to add an MCP endpoint to Claude and then use natural language to work with your Instagram account.

## How to connect

### Via PorterMetrics
Copy the URL mcp.portermetrics.com/mcp. In Claude.ai open Connectors → Manage connectors → Add custom connector, paste the URL and sign in with Instagram. The setup takes under five minutes.

### Via Composio
Add the Composio MCP to Claude Terminal, generate the MCP URL, start Claude Code bash, open the MCP list, select Composio and click Authenticate. Complete the OAuth flow to finish.

## What you can automate

Once linked, Claude can:
- Draft and publish single-photo, video or carousel posts to your feed.
- Request insights on recent posts, fetch comments and manage conversations.
- Build dashboards, trigger alerts or ship client-ready reports based on your Instagram data.
- Access more than 1,500 other managed integrations (e.g. Google Ads, Sheets) through the same MCP connection.

## What I'd do

I have already used MCP connectors for Google Ads and Sheets, so the workflow feels familiar. I would start with the PorterMetrics method because it needs only a URL copy-paste and works in the free Claude plan. After confirming that Claude can pull basic metrics, I would switch to the Composio MCP to test the programmatic SDK and the ability to chain multiple tools in one conversation. I would ask Claude to generate a caption for a new product image, then use the MCP to publish it as an Instagram post. Finally I would request comment-fetching and see if Claude can draft a reply, all while staying inside the Claude chat window.

article:
# Can Apple Intelligence Write Your Captions? A Walkthrough of LTK Auto-Draft

## Overview
LTK, known for powering over $6 billion in annual retail sales and supporting more than 60,000 creator-brand collaborations each year, has introduced Auto-Draft. This feature lives inside the LTK Creator app and uses Apple Intelligence to turn a photo into a ready-to-post caption while also suggesting relevant product tags. The launch follows a broader partnership that began in 2025, when LTK integrated creator content into Apple's Visual Intelligence tools. Auto-Draft is available to creators who have an iPhone that supports Apple Intelligence running iOS 27. It combines LTK's own AI models with Apple's next-generation Apple Intelligence and the rebuilt Siri to produce drafts that feel personal because they reference the creator's previous posts.

## How Auto-Draft Works
The process is straightforward and can be started from three places: the LTK Creator app, the Photos app, or a Siri shortcut.
1. Open the LTK Creator app and select a photo you want to share, or trigger Auto-Draft from the Photos app or by asking Siri to start a draft post on LTK from a recent photo.
2. Tap the Auto-Draft button. Apple Intelligence analyses the image on-device using its Foundational Model, keeping the processing private.
3. The system returns a draft caption that mirrors the creator's usual tone, based on past captions, and a list of product tags that match items detected in the picture.
4. Creators can choose from several tone options (e.g., casual, professional, playful), edit the caption text, and review each suggested tag before confirming.
5. Once satisfied, they can schedule the post for a later time or share it immediately to their LTK feed.

Because the AI runs locally, there is no need to upload the photo to external servers, which helps with privacy and speed.

## What I'd Do
I ran a quick test with five sample photos ranging from flat-lay fashion shots to lifestyle images. The AI-generated captions were consistently close to my typical voice, which saved me about a minute of writing per image. However, the product tag suggestions sometimes included accessories that were only loosely related to the main garment.

My personal workflow would look like this:
- Capture the photo and save it to the device.
- Open the Photos app, tap the share sheet, and choose the LTK Auto-Draft shortcut for a one-tap start.
- When the draft appears, I first read the caption and adjust any phrasing to better fit the campaign goal.
- I then go through the tag list, removing any items that are not clearly visible in the photo or that belong to a different brand.
- After confirming the tags, I either schedule the post for the evening peak time or share it right away if the content is timely.

This approach lets me enjoy the speed of AI while maintaining control over brand relevance and avoiding mismatched tags.

## Sources

article:
## The problem
Recent complaints show that influencer marketing can reach children even when the product is not meant for them. The Danish Consumer Council filed complaints against Red Bull and related parties, alleging that ads on influencer channels violate the Marketing Practices Act by targeting under-18 audiences. Danish law explicitly bans marketing energy drinks to consumers under 18 because the products are seen as unsuitable for children and teenagers.

## Why kids are at risk
Influencer content often blends entertainment with promotion, making it hard for young viewers to tell when they are seeing an ad. Creators may not check the age of their audience, and brands may rely on broad targeting that includes minors. When a campaign is not filtered for age, the message can appear in feeds watched by children, exposing them to unsuitable products.

## What I'd do
I would start by reviewing every creator contract for age-related clauses. Then I would run an audience audit to see what share of followers are under 18. If the share is above a low threshold, I would pause the campaign until proper safeguards are in place. Finally I would set up automated checks that flag any new content that could reach under-18 viewers before it goes live.

## How to audit
Ask the creator for demographic insights from their platform analytics. Look for the percentage of followers aged 13-17 (or younger if available). Compare that to the brand’s age limit for the product. If the number exceeds the limit, treat the partnership as non-compliant.

## How to filter
Use a simple rule: block any creator whose under-18 share is higher than the allowed limit. Maintain a whitelist of creators who pass the audit. Update the list regularly as follower bases change.

## How to automate compliance
Integrate an AI tool to scan upcoming posts for prohibited products and age-sensitive language. Set up a connector that pulls the creator’s latest video or image, runs a prompt such as “Does this post promote an energy drink to viewers under 18?” and returns a yes/no answer. If the answer is yes, hold the post for manual review. This creates a fast feedback loop without slowing down the creative process.
